<0>prompt-kit</0> is a well-made set of pieces: a chat container that sticks to the bottom, a prompt input, Markdown, reasoning, sources and a tool call. What happens when something goes wrong is up to you. Its Tool component, for instance, shows a call as streaming, ready, done or failed, with no state for a call that waits for approval. Its Prompt Input sends on Enter without checking whether an input method is still composing, and its File Upload handles dropping files but not upload progress or a failed upload.

Use prompt-kit when you want free, small pieces for a chat and plan to design the screens and their failure states yourself. Use HextaUI when you want the chat thread, the composer, the tool calls and the settings pages already built, with errors, retries, stops and approvals worked out. Both install with the shadcn CLI and share the shadcn/ui theme tokens, so you can mix them.
When prompt-kit is the better choice

prompt-kit components and their HextaUI counterparts
prompt-kit gives you free components for an AI chat. HextaUI gives you finished screens with stop, retry, failed replies, tool approvals and uploads handled.

prompt-kit gives you the pieces of an AI chat, such as a message, a prompt input and a tool call, as free shadcn/ui components. HextaUI gives you the finished screens those pieces become, with the hard states already handled. This page compares them as of October 2026.
